title: Acme Robotics - Embeddings & Rerank Discovery
next_steps: Send hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet
Share security SOC2 and architecture notes
Schedule 2-hour deep-dive benchmark with Arjun and Carlos next week
action_items: Maya Patel: Send pricing and starter configs by 2027-08-13
Arjun Singh: Prepare benchmark checklist + sample dataset by 2027-08-18
Carlos Mendes (Acme): Provide 1M sample vectors export by 2027-08-16
summary: Discovery to understand Acme Robotics' current vector search stack, scale and latency targets, and security/compliance constraints. Customer currently uses Pinecone + OpenAI embeddings and is evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a reranking pipeline. Key concerns: throughput (500 qps), latency for rerank (<150ms end-to-end), vector dimensionality (512 vs 1536), hybrid search with BM25, and VPC/KMS requirements. Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, and a hands-on benchmark session.
topics: hybrid search (BM25 + ANN) and reranking flow
security and compliance (SOC2, audit logs, SSO)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. We'll just do a quick intros, then dig into your current stack and the rerank use case. I'm Maya, AE for Redwood.
[00:32] Liam (Acme): Hey Maya, hi Arjun, thanks. Liam here, head of ML at Acme Robotics. We have Priya and Carlos on the call as well.
[01:05] Priya (Acme): Hi all, Priya, backend lead.
[01:18] Carlos (Acme): Carlos, data engineering.
[01:30] Arjun (Redwood SE): Hi, Arjun from Redwood. I'll aim to cover architecture and benchmarking details. Quick note, I might drop into more detail on dedupe and cache.
[01:55] Maya: Great. Liam, can you walk us through the current flow and where you're seeing pain?
[02:20] Liam: Sure. So right now we use OpenAI ada-ish embeddings for product-recall and Pinecone for vector storage. Our pipeline is a small hybrid search: BM25 on Elasticsearch for initial pass, then top-200 vectors from Pinecone, then a neural rerank using a BERT cross-encoder running on CPU infra. It's... fine, but cost is spiking and latency is a problem on peak.
[02:52] Priya: To add, our QPS spikes during shift changes for robots, and those 200-rerank calls are the cost sink. We're also concerned about vendor lock with OpenAI/Pinecone.
[03:20] Arjun: Understood. What's your latency SLO for the rerank end-to-end?
[03:35] Liam: Ideally under 150ms for top-5 final result; currently we're seeing p95 at around 420ms on peak.
[03:52] Maya: Ok, that's helpful. Do you have numbers on throughput targets? QPS sustained and burst?
[04:10] Carlos: Sustained target is about 200 qps, burst to 500 qps for 10-20 minute windows. Dataset size is roughly 40 million embeddings; most queries look at a recent sliding window of 1-2 million.
[04:36] Priya: Also worth noting, our embeddings are 512 dims today from OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002, but we'd like to experiment with higher dims (e.g., 1536) if we self-host to improve recall for domain-specific firmware docs.
[04:58] Arjun: Cool. A couple threads to unpack — vector dimensionality affects storage, ANN index choices, and latency; higher dims increase compute for distance ops but sometimes improve recall. For rerank, you also have to weigh cross-encoder cost vs using a lightweight hybrid scoring.
[05:25] Liam: Right; we're trying to evaluate two approaches: keep the cross-encoder but move it to dedicated GPU infra or replace it with a cheaper symmetric reranker plus thresholding.
[05:44] Maya: From Redwood's side we support hosted embeddings + search flow and also Dedicated capacity where you can have reserved GPU pools for the rerank model and high-throughput ANN serving. Private deployment is an option if you need VPC or air-gapped control.
[06:05] Priya: Security question up front: we need SOC2, SSO via SAML, and the ability to use our KMS. How does Redwood handle that across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[06:25] Arjun: Hosted: SOC2 plus customer isolation but we don't support customer-managed KMS in hosted tier today — we can encrypt at rest with our keys. Dedicated: you get tenant isolation and can integrate with customer KMS in many cases; Private: full control, VPC peering, customer KMS/HSM and audit log forwarding. We'll share the exact matrix in the security packet.
[06:52] Liam: Okay good. Cost is huge for us — especially the cross-encoder calls. Do you have typical unit economics for rerank + embeddings?
[07:09] Maya: We'll send a pricing sheet, but ballpark: hosted token/embedding pricing and then a per-GPU-hour for dedicated. We also provide model suggestions to reduce cost — e.g., smaller bi-encoders for candidate filtering, then a light cross-encoder only on top-10. That often gets you close on accuracy without the full top-200 rerank.
[07:36] Carlos: For the ANN layer, we currently rely on Pinecone managed indexes. If we moved to Redwood Dedicated, would we use your index layer or still point to Pinecone?
[07:52] Arjun: Redwood doesn't force a specific vector DB. For hosted flows we can integrate with Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, or you can push embeddings to a Redwood-managed index. For Dedicated/Private we often recommend colocating an ANN like FAISS/IVF/OPQ or Milvus on the same infra to minimize cross-network latency. There's config for index types (HNSW, IVF-PQ) and we can tune for memory vs latency.
[08:26] Priya: Interesting. How about hybrid search? We want BM25 staging then ANN retrieval — is there support for combining scores?
[08:42] Arjun: Yes — we support hybrid rerank pipelines. You can do a BM25 scoring pass, get top N, then ANN candidates with either Pinecone or FAISS, then do feature fusion and pass to a reranker. Redwood has builtin hooks for scoring fusion and we expose tracing to show per-route breakdown.
[09:05] Liam: Are there common gotchas in hybrid configs?
[09:12] Arjun: A few — score normalization between BM25 and cosine distances, keeping consistent recall by varying N, and ensuring your ANN recall at 512 dims is acceptable. Also watch index refresh strategies if your sliding window is changing fast — incremental indexing vs rebuilds.
[09:40] Priya: On the dimensionality question — what's the impact moving from 512 to 1536 on storage and query latency for HNSW?
[09:53] Arjun: Rough numbers: 3x the storage for raw vectors, but with PQ/OPQ you can compress; query latency increases modestly because the inner loop is larger, but for GPU-backed ANN the difference can be smaller depending on kernel optimizations. We can do an eval on your data to be precise.
[10:20] Maya: Let's talk throughput architecture: you said 200 sustained and 500 burst. For hosted, we'd probably recommend a burstable dedicated pool or pipelined approach where candidate retrieval is parallelized. For dedicated you'd reserve capacity tuned to hit 500 qps p95.
[10:44] Carlos: For the rerank model, is Redwood able to host proprietary models? We want to bring our in-house cross-encoder.
[10:54] Arjun: Yes — Dedicated and Private allow customer model artifacts. For Hosted we have curated models; you can bring-your-own model in Dedicated or Private. We support containerized deployments and GPU scheduling and can help with quantization and fp16/kernels.
[11:18] Liam: On quantization — we tried 8-bit quant on a trial; quality dropped a little. Have you seen that and what are your recommendations?
[11:30] Arjun: 8-bit can be ok for bi-encoders; for cross-encoders it's riskier. We recommend mixed approach: quantize candidate encoders, keep cross-encoder in fp16 on a small reserved GPU fleet. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles per-workload.
[11:55] Priya: How does the KV cache help in this flow? We do a lot of similar queries per robot type.
[12:05] Arjun: KV cache isn't exactly for embeddings; it's more for autoregressive models. But for embedding/ANN workflows we have result-level caching — prefix caching for repeated queries, and candidate cache which can save a lot if your query distribution repeats.
[12:28] Maya: Let's capture some acceptance criteria — Liam, what would make this a successful pilot?
[12:36] Liam:Three things: 1) Match or improve recall on our benchmark dataset; 2) Hit p95 latency under 150ms for rerank-new flow at 200 sustained qps; 3) Demonstrate cost savings vs current Pinecone + OpenAI stack.
[12:56] Maya: Perfect. That gives us a concrete POC success criteria. We'll propose a 2-4 week pilot.
[13:10] Carlos: For the POC, we can give a 1M subset and the rerank labels. Any preferences on dataset format?
[13:20] Arjun: CSV with id, vector (base64 or comma separated), metadata, and queries with gold labels is fine. We'll provide a sample template.
[13:34] Priya: How about monitoring — we need per-route token cost, latency, and error traces.
[13:44] Maya: Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, token and cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks. For Dedicated/Private you can forward logs to your SIEM and we support audit log forwarding.
[14:05] Liam: One more security note — we have to pass a security review in the month; is Redwood able to provide network diagrams and pen-test reports?
[14:17] Arjun: Yes. We'll include SOC2 attestation, pen-test summaries, and an architecture diagram for hosted and private. We can also export the onboarding checklist for your security team.
[14:37] Maya: I want to go into the rerank micro-arch a bit. Arjun, can you sketch a candidate architecture for them?
[14:45] Arjun: Sure. Flow A: Query -> BM25 top1k -> ANN top200 -> bi-encoder fast scoring -> top50 -> cross-encoder rerank top10 -> final. Flow B (cost-optimized): Query -> ANN top500 -> bi-encoder for scoring -> top20 -> lightweight cross-encoder or heuristic rerank top5. We'd recommend A for highest quality, B for cost-sensitive.
[15:15] Priya: What's the typical cost delta between A and B?
[15:21] Maya: It depends on model size and frequency, but B can be 40-60% cheaper on rerank GPU hours because it reduces cross-encoder invocations by an order of magnitude.
[15:36] Carlos: For the ANN layer we sometimes see cold-start latency on index sharding. Can Redwood help with warmers?
[15:45] Arjun: Yes. For dedicated pools we can prewarm page cache, keep indexes hot in memory, and set up a warm-up query set. We can also provide an autoscale policy that only scales with a short buffer to avoid cold starts.
[16:08] Liam: If we wanted a quick experiment, what's the fastest POC path? Hosted or Dedicated?
[16:16] Maya: Fastest to deliver results is Hosted with Redwood-managed ANN and embeddings; limited to our certified models and no customer KMS. If you need KMS or VPC, Dedicated gets you faster control without full private install; Private is longer due to network setup.
[16:38] Priya: Do you have benchmark examples we can review?
[16:44] Arjun: Yes, we'll share examples — comparable benchmarks with dimensions, index types, recall/latency tradeoffs. We'll also propose a benchmark run on your sample data to be objective.
[17:00] Liam: On the vector storage side, are there read replicas or geo-replication options? Some of our deployments are global.
[17:10] Arjun: For hosted we have region-aware routing and replication strategies. For Dedicated you can setup regional clusters or have cross-region read replicas depending on latency needs. For Private you'd control deployment topology.
[17:30] Priya: Any limits on vector count per index on Redwood-managed indexes?
[17:38] Arjun: Practically we handle tens of millions per index; for 40M we recommend sharded indexes and careful param tuning. We can share sample configs.
[17:55] Carlos: A slightly odd question — do you do rerank determinism testing? We need reproducible top-k for A/B tests.
[18:04] Arjun: We provide traceability and you can pin model seeds and versions. For index nondeterminism (HNSW), you can fix seeds and use deterministic build policies for tests. We'll show configuration examples.
[18:26] Maya: Switching to integration — what does the integration look like for our engineers, Priya?
[18:33] Priya: We prefer minimal infra changes. Ideally a few API calls to Redwood or an option to point Redwood at our Pinecone data.
[18:45] Arjun: Both are supported — you can push embeddings to Redwood via API or keep them in Pinecone and call Redwood for rerank. If you move to Dedicated, colocating index and rerank reduces latency.
[19:02] Liam: What's the SLA on Dedicated? We need uptime for robots.
[19:10] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA options; typical is 99.9% with support SLAs for incident response. We'll include SLA terms in the contract draft.
[19:26] Priya: Any hidden costs we should know about? Egress, logging retention?
[19:33] Maya: Storage and egress are line items. Logging/observability retention over the default window is an add-on. We'll be transparent in the pricing sheet.
[19:47] Carlos: For the POC dataset we'll likely hand over 1M vectors. Do you have an ingestion best practice?
[19:55] Arjun: Yes — bulk ingest in batched chunks, use parquet or ndjson, and parallelize uploader clients. If you have metadata-heavy records, we recommend denormalizing small payloads to avoid join-time costs.
[20:16] Liam: Legal question — is there a standard DPA and can we get data residency guarantees?
[20:24] Maya: We have standard DPA, and for Private/Dedicated we can guarantee data residency by deploying in a chosen region or your private VPC. Hosted is region-scoped but we can discuss contractual residency commitments.
[20:42] Priya: On monitoring again, can we hook Redwood traces into Datadog?
[20:49] Arjun: Yes, we support log forwarding to Datadog, Splunk, and S3, plus metrics via Prometheus endpoints in Dedicated/Private.
[21:05] Maya: Are there any blockers from your side for starting a pilot?
[21:12] Liam: No major blockers, just internal signoff and a security review timeline. If we get the security packet quickly we can slot the POC next week.
[21:26] Maya: Great. We'll aim to send the security and pricing docs today and propose two POC windows.
[21:36] Priya: Can we get a rough estimate of the engineering effort to set up the POC?
[21:44] Arjun: For a hosted POC, minimal — a couple API calls and a vector export, maybe 1-2 engineer days. For Dedicated POC with model hosting, expect 3-5 days of setup and syncs.
[22:03] Carlos: For the reranker model, do you support GPUs in different classes? like A100 vs T4?
[22:12] Arjun: Yes; Dedicated supports a range of GPU types. We can recommend A100 for large cross-encoders for latency-sensitive workloads, T4 for smaller cost-optimized models.
[22:30] Maya: Anything else we should capture?
[22:34] Liam: One final note — we care about cold-starts for new firmware pushes; we might need a continuous ingestion pipeline.
[22:42] Arjun: We can set up incremental indexing pipelines and near-realtime ingestion; there are trade-offs on indexing latency vs recall. We'll propose a config.
[23:00] Priya: Ok that's helpful. I have one question — do you provide connectors for CDC from Postgres?
[23:08] Arjun: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can provide connectors or recommend Debezium-based flows. For hosted you'll push deltas via API.
[23:20] Maya: We're approaching the top of the hour — let's recap and assign owners.
[23:28] Maya: Action item recap: Maya send pricing + security docs; Arjun prepare benchmark plan; Acme (Carlos) share 1M sample vectors. Target dates in the action items.
[23:45] Liam: Sounds good.
[23:50] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[24:00] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up by EOD with the packet and proposed POC dates.
[24:10] (call ends)

Note: transcription has occasional mis-hearings — e.g., references to "ada-ish" embeddings, "kt cache" (transcribed from KV cache) and some product names may be slightly off in auto transcript.
